name: application-retention-curve-chart
title: Retention Curve Chart
description: A decaying percentage-retained line chart over days-since-signup, with a cohort selector for comparing how different signup cohorts retain over time.
useWhen: Tracking how a percentage of users remain active over days/weeks since signup, the classic product-analytics retention curve shape.
Comparing retention across multiple signup cohorts (by month, by acquisition channel) via a selector above the chart.
avoidWhen: You need a grid of retention percentages across many cohorts at once — `Cohort Retention Grid` (heatmap table) fits that comparison better than a single line.
The metric isn't naturally a decaying percentage over time since a fixed start event — a generic line chart from `charts` fits other trend shapes better.
responsiveBehavior: The chart is a single SVG with viewBox scaling that shrinks proportionally with its container; the cohort selector tabs wrap or scroll horizontally on narrow viewports rather than shrinking below a legible tap target.
accessibility: The cohort selector buttons use aria-pressed to indicate the active cohort, not solely a background color change.
Each data point is marked with a visible dot in addition to the connecting line, aiding precise reading of values at labeled days.
Day-since-signup labels (Day 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 30) are shown as text below the axis, not solely inferred from x-position.

variants.title: Cohort retention curve
variants.description: A retention curve decaying from 100% at Day 0 to a ~22% plateau by Day 30, with data-point dots, a shaded area, and a three-cohort selector (Jun/May/Apr, Jun active).
accessibility: The active cohort tab carries aria-pressed="true" and a distinct raised background.

variants.title: Cohort retention curve (Dark)
variants.description: Retention curve chart adapted for dark surfaces, with line and area colors re-tuned for dark contrast.
accessibility: Line, area fill, and cohort tab text all meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark card background.
